title: Rings that share boundary: build a ring or surface segment from stretches of existing rings plus new anchors
description:
User request 2026-10-04: not every part is a ring around a limb. Segmenting a patch of surface (a muscle, a pec, a plate on the carapace) means drawing a boundary that exactly follows parts of existing rings and then cuts across new surface. Today the user has to fight the anchor placement to retrace an existing ring, and never matches it exactly. Wanted: a sub-tool in the ring tool where the user picks two points on an existing ring (or on several rings) to take the stretch between them, chains stretches from multiple rings, and adds new anchors where the boundary leaves them; the new ring reuses those stretches exactly (the same surface path, so the region flood sees one shared wall, no slivers), and closes into a segment. Store it so that editing the source ring keeps the shared stretch in sync, or explicitly snapshots it; decide and document which. This is how non-ring 'surface segments' get made.

Rework 2026-10-07 (user review of the B-key shared ring): the interaction is wrong. Clicking a ring twice for a stretch is unintuitive, and the tool only bridges two rings across the big leftover region; it cannot split a region within itself (e.g. region 28 on a leg, a tube between two rings). The user's model: SPLIT A REGION WITH CUTS. Click points on a region's boundary in any order; the tool pairs them into cuts across the region and splits it. Two points split a region one cut can split (a disc-like patch); where one cut cannot (a tube between two rings: one ring-to-ring cut only opens it into a sheet), four points give two cuts and two pieces. Click order must not matter: the tool tries the pairings and takes the one whose cuts do not cross and actually split the region, previewing the result in region colours before Enter. The big leftover region is not special: it splits like any other. A cut is an open curve whose two ends lie on existing walls (rings or earlier cuts) - which is CRAW-53's open groove cut - so this rework absorbs CRAW-53. Regions then follow from the existing region flood with cuts as walls; no composed closed loops are needed. Keep what carries over from the first pass: RingAttachment (a cut's ends linked to their source wall, so editing the ring moves the cut), open spline tracing (SurfaceSplineTracer.open), shared-edge walls without slivers, the required metric= wiring. Drop the stretch/compose model (SharedBoundaryRing, shared_ring) unless something still needs it.

Rework 2026-10-14 (user review of the K split): keep it inside the ring tool's K mode, renamed BISECTOR ("K: bisect"). The user found: X left the split instead of deleting points; cuts named their walls by DSL label, so an unsaved ring could not be a wall ("Ctrl+S first"); the algorithm was unclear and points had to land within a few pixels of the clicked region's edge; the region was fixed by the face under the first click, so walls were one-sided and click order mattered; a cut could not run across several regions, so the crawfish scales took 26 cuts (~30 clicks); cuts crossed themselves. Wanted: a bisector is an open geodesic spline (the ring tracer, open) through user anchors, its two ends snapped to the nearest ring or bisector within a generous reach, anchors anywhere in between to steer it, a hover preview, crossing any walls on the way and splitting every region it crosses, joinable to rings and other bisectors; walls named by in-memory identity and resolved to labels only at Ctrl+S; X/Delete/Backspace delete a point, Esc leaves; a self-crossing draft shown invalid and not confirmable. The 2-or-4-point pairing model (RegionSplit) is retired; a tube between two rings takes two bisectors.
definition-of-done: BISECTOR REWORK (2026-10-14, replaces R1-R7): B1. K in the ring tool toggles the bisector (no new tool); hint, status and log say "bisect" and name the algorithm (open geodesic spline through the anchors, traced like a ring). B2. Each end snaps to the nearest ring or bisector vertex within 40 px; clicks after both ends add steering anchors anywhere, placed where the traced spline comes out shortest without crossing itself; the hover previews the bisector from the first end to the cursor (magenta, black when it would end off a wall or cross itself). B3. X, Delete and Backspace delete the selected point, else the last (inner anchors, then the second end, then the first); Esc leaves. B4. Walls are named by in-memory ring serial; an unsaved ring is a wall; Ctrl+S writes walls first and every bisector after its walls, ends resolved to labels then; save + reload gives identical regions. B5. Click order and the side of a ring the first click lands on do not change the bisector. B6. One bisector may cross walls and splits every region it crosses; it is saved as ONE spline_cut statement; RingRegions takes it as a wall once both ends lie on walls, and its crossings are not reported as problems. B7. Bisectors join rings and each other and close regions. B8. A self-crossing bisector is drawn invalid and Enter refuses it. B9. On a crawfish copy the tail scales (the user's 14 side cuts) are done with two bisectors; screenshots in tmp/craw-bisector-*.png. B10. Tests in BisectorTest cover X, unsaved walls + save/reload, click order, two regions split by one bisector, joins, no self-crossing.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test on a simple mesh: a patch bounded by stretches of two rings plus one new span; region count and no slivers. 2. Live on a tmp copy of the crawfish: segment one carapace plate using existing rings; screenshots.
changes-made: Built in worktree craw-49 (uncommitted). Ring tool: B starts a shared ring; click a ring twice to take the stretch between the two points (shorter arc, F flips to the other), click off rings to add anchors to the span after the last stretch, Backspace drops the last piece, Enter confirms, Ctrl+S saves; clicking a confirmed shared ring re-opens it. Saved as one statement ring_NN = shared_ring(geometry=..., pieces="ring_63: from / via / to; x,y,z; ring_62: from / via / to", label=...) (SharedRingNode). LINKED, not a snapshot: a stretch stores its source label and three points, re-attached to the source's edge loop on every evaluation (RingAttachment, the shared attach piece CRAW-53's open cuts should reuse together with SurfaceSplineTracer.open), so editing a source re-composes every shared ring on it (tool: SharedRingDraft.followSource on confirm; reload: graph order). Deleting a source a shared ring uses is refused. SharedBoundaryRing.compose walls exactly the source's own loop edges between the stretch ends, traces spans as open splines snapped to edges, trims a span where it runs along a wall so no pocket forms, joins anchorless stretch-to-stretch junctions at the vertex the two rings share, and refuses a loop that meets itself. RingRegions no longer reports edges two rings share as a touch. Tests: SharedBoundaryRingTest (patch of two crossing-ring stretches plus one span on a tube: 5 regions, no region under 40 faces, each shared stretch one unbroken run of the source's own edges; one-stretch patch; linked edit of the source; DSL round trip through RingDslWriter and the node). mvn test 427 pass. Fertility 13 ring fingerprints identical to master (RingAnchorOrderBenchmark on a master export); crawfish 82 rings adopted with no refusal. Live on tmp/crawfish_shared.dsl: ring_85 from stretches of ring_63 and ring_62 plus one anchor, region 41 bounded by exactly ring_62, ring_63, ring_85 (650 faces), every region next to ring_85 at least 650 faces; screenshots tmp/craw-shared-draft.png, tmp/craw-shared-regions.png.

Rework 2026-10-07 (worktree craw-49, uncommitted): split a region with cuts replaces the B-key shared ring. Removed SharedBoundaryRing, SharedRingNode (shared_ring), SharedRingDraft and their test; ConformingLoopSnap is master again. Ring tool: K starts a split; click points on a region's edge (just inside it) in any order; region colours turn on and preview the resulting regions, the cuts draw pink; Backspace drops the last point, Enter confirms (one undoable edit), X/Esc/K drops the split. Pairing rule (RegionSplit): the region is the one the region colours show under the first point; each point snaps to the nearest edge vertex that has an interior neighbour (refused with a distance when too far); points are sorted by vertex id so click order cannot matter; every pairing of 2 or 4 points is tried (1 or 3), each cut is a shortest path through the region's interior off every wall, a later cut may not touch an earlier one (crossing pairings fail); kept: the pairing adding the fewest pieces (>0), then the shortest. Refusals carry a reason, e.g. "a cut from ring_05 to ring_07 joins two of the region's 2 boundary loops, which only opens it; click two more points". Cuts are open splines (SurfaceSplineTracer.open) through anchors spaced along that path, densified until they stay inside the region; SurfaceSpline.cut keeps the longest run of the snapped edge path touching its end walls only at its ends (no pocket/sliver at the junction). RingRegions: an open ring walls the flood as a cut (ringIsCut) once each loose end lies on another wall (fixpoint, so cuts may end on cuts); cuts have no sides, are no handle, and their attached ends are no touch. Saved one statement per cut: ring_NN = spline_cut(geometry=..., metric=surface.metric, points="...", ends="ring_a; ring_b", label=...) (SplineCutNode; ends re-attach to the named walls' nearest vertex on every evaluation = linked). A confirmed cut reopens as a draft like a ring (R6): add anchors (inserted where they lengthen it least), drag them (ends slide along their wall), delete inner ones; confirming an edited ring re-attaches every cut ending on it; deleting a wall a cut ends on is refused. New automation route `ixdar-cli rings split --points ... [--region N] [--confirm]`. Verified on tmp/crawfish copy (absorbed numbering): tube region 37 (ring_05/ring_07, 2 loops) four points -> 2 cuts, pieces 9129/24996, same fingerprints in 4 click orders; two points ring_05->ring_07 refused with the reason above; disc-like region 49 (ring_55/ring_69, 1 loop) two points -> 1 cut, 982/758; largest region 66 (91706 faces) four points -> 19242/72464; unabsorbed 300->302 regions with slivers unchanged (206) and no problem naming a cut; save + reload identical region faces; reopened cut took an anchor; editing ring_55 moved the linked cut end, save/reload identical. Ring fingerprints: fertility 13/13 equal master, crawfish 82/82 equal. Region 28 in this fixture state is not a clean leg tube (it touches ring_60 only on a short arc, bounded mostly by ring_48/ring_14), so the tube check used region 37. RegionSplitTest (4): tube four points any order, two ring-to-ring points refused, disc patch two points, spline_cut statement reloads identical edges. mvn test 452 pass. Screenshots tmp/craw-split-tube-preview.png, tmp/craw-split-tube-confirmed.png, tmp/craw-split-largest-preview.png, tmp/craw-cut-anchor-added.png, tmp/craw-cut-follows-ring.png.

Bisector rework 2026-10-14 (worktree craw-49, uncommitted on top of the branch commit "ree" the user made of the previous diff). Synced onto master after CRAW-63 (crease newDraftMode, red/purple preview colours and per-ring confirmedMode kept). Renamed split -> bisector everywhere the user sees it and in code: RegionSplit retired (deleted), RingTool.splitting/split/startSplit/placeSplitPoint/replanSplit/leaveSplit/tracedCut -> bisecting/startBisector/placeBisectorEnd/leaveBisector/tracedBisector, confirmedCutEnds/draftCutEnds -> confirmedBisectorEnds/draftBisectorEnds (int serials), SurfaceSpline.cut -> SurfaceSpline.bisector, RingDslWriter.appendCut/rewriteCut/cutStatement -> appendBisector, route /mesh/rings/split (Split) -> /mesh/rings/bisect (Bisect, `ixdar-cli rings bisect --points "end; anchors...; end" [--confirm]`), RegionSplitTest -> BisectorTest. The DSL node stays spline_cut (SplineCutNode) so existing files, IMG_4111's 26 cuts included, load unchanged.
(1) X, Delete and Backspace on a bisector delete the selected point, else the last: inner anchors, then the second end (the first then waits), then the first; on a re-opened confirmed bisector the last end deletes it. Esc and K leave the bisector; an open bisector draft stays for Enter.
(2) No DSL tie: each confirmed ring has an in-memory serial (confirmedRingSerial, kept in undo states, re-used when the graph re-runs and re-adopts the same label); bisector ends name walls by serial. Unsaved rings are walls. Ctrl+S writes rings first, then every live bisector (removed and re-appended under its own id, each after the bisectors it ends on) with ends resolved to labels at that moment. Audit: no other refusal waits on a save; the remaining DSL-keyed things are graph rings that adoption refuses (drawn from marks, not walls a bisector can snap to) and the region tool's hidden/selected state, keyed by live labels that change from "ring #N" to ring_NN at save.
(3) Algorithm: an open geodesic spline through the anchors, traced by SurfaceSplineTracer (open) like rings, walls = its snapped edge path. Ends snap to the nearest ring/bisector vertex within 40 px by a walk out from the cursor vertex (stamped scratch arrays, wall map rebuilt only when rings change, no full-mesh scan); RingAttachment.attach no longer allocates a vertex-sized array. After both ends, clicks add steering anchors anywhere, inserted in the span where the traced spline comes out shortest and simple. Hover previews the bisector from the first end to the snapped cursor (magenta; black when it would end off a wall, cross itself or wall nothing); the hint and status rows name the algorithm.
(4) No region model: the first click picks no region; walls are two-sided; click order and the ring side of the first click do not change the result (the lower vertex leads).
(5) One bisector may cross walls; saved as ONE spline_cut per bisector (simplest: one edge mask is one wall for RingRegions, which already walls an open ring whose loose ends lie on walls, so every region it crosses splits and reload is the same statement; splitting per region would need crossing-point bookkeeping and many statements). SurfaceSpline.bisector keeps crossings of its own end walls (the old longest-run trim dropped all but one region) and trims only touches within 4 edges of an end (pocket guard). RingRegions no longer reports a bisector crossing a wall (RingAttachment.crossesAt, a fan-order test) as "cross" or "touch". Bisectors join rings and other bisectors (ends snap onto either).
(6) Self-crossing, measured on the tube fixture with the new open-path SurfacePathCrossings: anchors densely along a staircase edge path, every 32..1 vertices: 0 crossings; ends + two anchors in click order [A, far, near, B]: 1 crossing; the same anchors at their least-length places [A, near, far, B]: 0. The old code also never checked a cut for crossing (reportDraft treated every cut as simple, drags and inserts skipped the check). Fix: anchors are inserted at the shortest simple place, drags that would cross are refused, every bisector draft is checked, a crossing one draws black and Enter refuses it.
(7) The 2/4-point pairing model is gone; a tube band between two rings takes two bisectors.
Verified live on tmp/crawfish_scales.dsl (IMG_4111 without the 26 cuts): the tail scales split by 2 bisectors from ring_06 to ring_05 across ring_04/02/01/00/03, 5 points each (2 ends + 3 steering anchors; 2 ends alone run diagonally across the lobes) = 10 clicks for the user's 14 side cuts; each of the 6 tail bands splits belly from lobes; 36-116 ms per edit; Ctrl+S appended 2 spline_cut statements; restart on the saved file: 191 regions, identical face counts. Residual: one "ring_00 and ring_55 touch at 1 vertex" problem where the bisector grazes crease ring_00 next to its crossing. Screenshots tmp/craw-bisector-hover-preview.png, tmp/craw-bisector-scales-preview.png, tmp/craw-bisector-scales-confirmed.png; the launch entry's tmp/crawfish_shared.dsl now holds that saved result. BisectorTest (6): X deletes points then Esc leaves; unsaved ring walls + save order + spline_cut statement reloads identical edges + re-adoption keeps serials; 4 click orders/sides give identical edges; one bisector across two patches splits both (5 regions, no sliver, no problem); bite + join close regions; click-order anchors cross and Enter refuses. mvn test 488 pass.
